label: Halves of the street-grid steps
subgoals: Average the two x-values for the middle x
Average the two y-values for the middle y
Keep horizontal-first order in the answer pair

slice.rule: The midpoint of two points is found by averaging each coordinate separately: add the two $x$-values and halve, add the two $y$-values and halve. Nothing else is involved — the midpoint is componentwise, not a new kind of average.

label: Origin and axes as reference points
subgoals: Start every address at the origin (0, 0)
Measure x along the horizontal axis
Measure y along the vertical axis

slice.rule: Coordinates are measured from the origin, with $x$ along the horizontal axis and $y$ along the vertical. Averaging works regardless of sign, because each coordinate is handled on its own axis.

label: Drill: middle of two addresses
subgoals: Add the two x-values and halve the total
Add the two y-values and halve the total
Check the midpoint sits halfway on each axis

slice.rule: Average the two $x$-values for the middle $x$, average the two $y$-values for the middle $y$, and write the pair in that order. Then check the result really is halfway on each axis.
